headline: Forced labour guidance, supplier data caps, and national right-to-repair moves
summary: The European Commission has published official guidelines under the Forced Labour Regulation, providing critical criteria for supply-chain risk assessments. Simultaneously, Brussels finalised streamlined ESRS standards alongside limits on data demands placed on mid-sized suppliers. National implementation of the Right to Repair Directive is also progressing, with Italy enforcing rules this month.

items.title: Commission publishes official Forced Labour Regulation guidelines
items.what: The European Commission released official guidelines detailing risk-based implementation and enforcement criteria under the EU Forced Labour Regulation.
items.meaning: Provides official reference criteria for auditing and engaging your 200 mainland Chinese suppliers, where trade and labour scrutiny is most acute.
items.action: Benchmark current Chinese supplier audit protocols against the Commission's newly published guidance criteria.

sources.title: Update on the EU Forced Labour Regulation: The European Commission's Guidelines Have Been Published

items.title: EU finalises streamlined ESRS and caps supplier sustainability data requests
items.what: The EU finalised streamlined reporting standards and introduced limits permitting suppliers with under 1,000 staff to refuse excessive sustainability data requests.
items.meaning: Restricts the volume of custom ESG data you can contractually demand from smaller Chinese manufacturers for CSRD compliance.
items.action: Align supplier data collection sheets with the new voluntary standards to minimise refusal risks.

items.title: Italy enacts EU Right to Repair Directive from 22 October
items.what: Italy announced the entry into force of national measures implementing the EU Right to Repair Directive on 22 October 2026.
items.meaning: As the brand owner and legal manufacturer, your power tools and garden equipment marketed in Italy must meet national repairability obligations.
items.action: Review spare parts availability, pricing, and repair documentation access for Italian distribution channels.

sources.title: Repair of goods: in Italia, the EU directive will come into force on 22 October

items.title: Regulators highlight ESMA 2026 recommendations for CSRD preparation
items.what: Securities regulators including France's AMF urged listed issuers to align reporting preparations with ESMA's 2026 sustainability statement recommendations.
items.meaning: Signals supervisory expectations on value-chain data quality and materiality ahead of your mandatory FY2027 CSRD reporting scope.
items.action: Review ESMA's focal points to ensure value chain due diligence systems meet audit expectations.

sources.title: Preparing upcoming sustainability statements: the AMF draws listed companies’ attention to ESMA’s 2026 recommendations
